source: Mission_Proposal_v14.docx: Ollama qwen2.5:7b extraction (2026-10-23, 22 requirements) corrected by hand: subject, 'mean' revisit, one need per requirement, reference cases and propagation added; used by FrontEnd/star_smoke_test.py

requirements.text: Each satellite shall re-enter the atmosphere within 5 years of the end of its mission.
The satellites shall keep a safe separation from each other, with a distance between any two satellites not below 5 km at any time.
The satellites shall orbit between 500 km and 650 km of altitude.
The mission lifetime shall be three years.
Each satellite shall be a CubeSat of 6U to 12U format, with a total mass within the maximum allowed by the CubeSat Design Specification for the selected format (12 kg for 6U and 24 kg for 12U).
Each satellite shall be three-axis stabilised with a pointing accuracy better than 0.1 deg and point nominally at nadir.
The attitude knowledge of each satellite shall be better than 0.03 deg during imaging.
Each satellite shall be able to slew by 30 deg in not more than 120 seconds.
Each satellite shall carry a visible-spectrum push-broom camera with a panchromatic Ground Sample Distance of 6.5 m and a swath of 23 km at nadir.
The camera shall image targets at an off-nadir angle of up to 30 deg with a GSD not exceeding 10 m at that angle.
Each satellite shall acquire images in daylight only and send them to the ground through UHF and S-band links.
Each satellite shall alternate imaging orbits and idle orbits: in a day of 15 orbits, 8 are imaging orbits and 7 are idle orbits, with downlink through the UHF or S-band transmitters.

The electrical power budget shall be closed in sunlight and in eclipse for every operating mode (idle, payload acquisition, UHF downlink and S-band downlink), with the duty cycle of each subsystem and a design margin of 10 percent.
The daily energy balance shall not be negative and the battery depth of discharge shall not exceed 30 percent in any orbit.

The platform components of each CubeSat (structure, on-board computer, electrical power system, battery, deployable solar panels, UHF and S-band radios, attitude determination and control subsystem and optical payload) shall be selected among commercially available CubeSat products documented by vendor datasheets, and together they shall fit within the mass and volume of the selected format.
The total mass of each satellite shall include a margin of 10 percent and the volume shall have a margin of at least 10 percent.
The temperatures of the CubeSat faces, solar panels, central body and battery shall be assessed along the orbit and during the daylight reference imaging pass.
The battery temperature of the CubeSat shall stay within its operational limit.
The type of orbit, the number of satellites and the number of orbital planes shall be optimised to minimise the revisit time and to maximise the coverage of the monuments.
The mean revisit time of each monument shall not exceed 48 hours.
Each monument shall be covered on at least 50 percent of the days of the evaluation period.
The satellites shall propagate the orbits for at least 7 days with the Earth oblateness (J2), the atmospheric drag and the solar radiation pressure.
The performance of the constellation shall be evaluated over a period of one week (7 days).
The design shall be checked on two reference cases over 48 hours starting on 21 May 2026 at 13:41 UTC.

In the first reference case, a satellite shall image the Colosseum in Rome in daylight, with an off-nadir angle not exceeding 30 deg and with the Sun above the horizon at the target, preferably higher than 20 deg.

In the second reference case, a satellite shall cross the sky of the ASI Space Geodesy Centre 'G. Colombo' at Matera at night, above 10 deg of elevation and illuminated by the Sun, while the Sun is more than 12 deg below the horizon at the site.
The peak apparent visual magnitude of every sunlit satellite seen from Matera at night shall be fainter than magnitude 7.

The light reflected by the satellite during the night pass shall be provided as a light curve with a time step not larger than 5 seconds, together with the phase angle, the range and the estimated apparent visual magnitude.
Compliance shall be verified by simulation and analysis only.
The applicant shall provide evidence of the optimised constellation architecture and its revisit-time and coverage performance over the monuments.
The applicant shall provide evidence of the propagated orbit and attitude of the satellites, the two reference passes, the separation between the satellites and the disposal delta-v.
